q:
The position–time graph of a particle on a straight line consists of two straight segments: from (t = 0, x = 0) to (t = 6 s, x = 25 m), and then to (t = 13 s, x = 4 m). Find its average speed over the whole 13 s.
Give the answer in m/s, correct to 2 decimal places.
s:
First segment: it moves 25 m forward.
Second segment: x falls from 25 m to 4 m, so it comes back 21 m.
Total distance = 25 + 21 = 46 m.
Average speed = 46 ÷ 13 = 3.54 m/s

q: A particle starts from rest and its acceleration changes with time as a = 2t (m/s², t in s). Find its velocity at t = 6 s.
s:
The acceleration is not constant, so integrate: v = ∫a dt.
v = ∫2t dt = 1t² + C
At t = 0, v = 0, so C = 0.
v = 1 × 6² = 36 m/s

q: A particle moves on a straight line according to x = t² − 8t (SI units). Find the total distance it covers from t = 0 to t = 5 s.
s:
v = dx/dt = 2t − 8, which is zero at t = 4 s, so it turns back there.
x(4) = 16 − 32 = −16 m, so the first part is 16 m.
x(5) = 25 − 40 = −15 m, so the second part is |−15 − (−16)| = 1 m.
Distance = 16 + 1 = 17 m

q:
A person walks 48 m due east and then 64 m due north in a total time of 12 s. Find the magnitude of the average velocity.
(Options are rounded to 2 decimal places.)
s:
Average velocity = displacement ÷ time (a vector quantity).
Displacement = √(48² + 64²) = √6400 = 80 m.
Average velocity = 80 ÷ 12 = 6.67 m/s

q:
A car covers the first half of a journey at 80 km h⁻¹ and the second half at 60 km h⁻¹ along the same straight road. What is its average speed for the whole journey?
(Options are rounded to 2 decimal places.)
s:
The two halves cover equal distances, so the times are different.
Let each half be d. Time = {d;80} + {d;60}.
Average speed = total distance ÷ total time = {2v₁v₂;v₁ + v₂}
= {2 × 80 × 60;80 + 60} = 68.57 km h⁻¹

q: The velocity–time graph of a particle is a straight line starting at 28 m/s at t = 0 and sloping down by 4 m/s every second (so the velocity becomes negative after some time). Find the displacement from t = 0 to t = 13 s.
s:
The velocity is v = 28 − 4t, and it is zero at t = 7 s.
Area above the axis (0 to 7 s): ½ × 7 × 28 = 98 m (positive).
Area below the axis (7 to 13 s): ½ × 6 × 24 = 72 m (negative).
Displacement = 98 − 72 = 26 m

x(3) = 162 m and x(7) = 98 m.

q:
On a velocity–time graph, a straight line joins the points (t = 2 s, v = 12 m/s) and (t = 10 s, v = 7 m/s). Find the magnitude of the acceleration represented by this line.
(Options are rounded to 2 decimal places.)
s:
The slope of a v–t graph is the acceleration.
Slope = {Δv;Δt} = {7 − 12;10 − 2} = {-5;8}
= −0.63 m/s²
The negative sign means retardation; the magnitude is asked.

s:
Differentiate twice: v = dx/dt and a = dv/dt.
v = 9t² − 2t
a = 18t − 2

q:
A particle moves along a straight line with v = 5 − 1t (in m/s, t in seconds). Find the total distance it travels from t = 0 to t = 11 s.
Give the answer in m.
s:
The particle stops and turns back when v = 0, i.e. at t = 5 ÷ 1 = 5 s.
Distance before turning = ½ × 5 × 5 = 12.5 m.
After turning, v at t = 11 s is -6 m/s, so distance = ½ × 6 × 6 = 18 m.
Distance travelled = 12.5 + 18 = 30.5 m

q: The position of a particle is x = t³ + 5t² + 11t (x in metres, t in seconds). Find its velocity at t = 3 s.
s:
Velocity is the derivative of position: v = dx/dt.
v = 3t² + 10t + 11
At t = 3: v = 3 × 9 + 10 × 3 + 11
v = 68 m/s
